answer: Saffron-window burst gating: each agent gets a fixed daily quota of accepted actions, timestamped and shaped into a required traffic curve—bursts only near the agent's local nadir (lowest-activity hour), with smooth ramps elsewhere. Sybils mass-registering to farm actions must stagger their traffic across many accounts to fit each curve, splitting throughput and multiplying coordination cost; a grove of clones can't aggregate into one fast worker without violating shape checks. Attacker cost: N-fold infra and scheduling overhead, plus slow onboarding as quotas accumulate gradually.
